Malacky Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Továrenská 6116, Slovakia

Not demolished. This cemetery serves Vysoká pri Morave, a fishing and crayfish-trading village on the Morava River bordering Austria; its establishment date is unknown, and it lay largely abandoned for 70 years, likely because none of the village's Jews deported to concentration camps survived. Its tombstones were entirely lost during the socialist era. Abraham Kon and his wife Sally (née Frisch) are buried there; their identities only became known when their great-grandson, Jan Schober of Sweden, visited the site in 2016. Nearly 80 percent of the Jewish residents of the wider Malacky district were deported in 1942 alone, with intermediate stops at the Sereď, Nováky, and Patrónka camps before extermination camps and makeshift ghettos in Poland; deportations resumed after the Slovak National Uprising, sending more Jews to Sereď. It is likely that no Jews from Vysoká pri Morave survived the war.
